prompt:
Refer to the four attached full-body images of women and generate one square 4-panel image to be used as material for a fashion video.

[Final Form]
The overall aspect ratio is 1:1. Divide the screen into an even 2x2 grid, making each panel square. Place one woman in each panel for a total of four. In order of attachment, 1st = top left, 2nd = top right, 3rd = bottom left, 4th = bottom right. No outer borders, gaps between panels, or 3D frames are needed.

This is a modern fashion campaign featuring a sharp contrast between text size, solid fill and outlines, and overlapping versus empty space, using a limited range of elements. Keep the person's area clean and create a rich, art-directed composition for the text area. This is a poster image to be used as final video material. It should be a finished design, not a mockup. Each of the four images must stand as a complete poster on its own while maintaining unity as a whole.

[Maintaining Reference Subject: Priority Conditions Over Placement]
This is a common instruction set corresponding to the four full-body images of women provided by the user. Do not pre-set specific faces, body types, outfits, or hairstyles. The information for the person in each panel must come only from the image corresponding to that panel. Do not mix features or standardize the four women to a common face or model body type.

Maintain facial contours, eye/nose/mouth shapes and placement, expression, age, skin tone, hairstyle, and hair color exactly as shown in the reference. Maintain head-to-body ratio, neck length, shoulder width, torso length/width, hip width, limb length/thickness, and hand/foot size. Do not perform body corrections such as slimming the face, thinning the torso, lengthening legs, or stretching the body. Maintain the subject's pose, face/body orientation, gaze, arm/hand/leg positions, stance, and weight distribution. Do not flip horizontally. Carry over the shape, color, material, length, fit, and key folds or silhouettes of clothing, shoes, and accessories. Do not misinterpret loose clothing contours as body contours. Do not carry over the background, text, or borders of the reference photos.

[Method for Placing Subjects in Space]
Treat the person and clothing as a single unit, scaling them uniformly to place them. Do not apply different scaling to parts like the face, torso, or legs. Adjust placement while preserving the original silhouette rather than redrawing the pose to fit the frame. Ensure the entire outline, from top of head to soles of shoes, including hair and fingertips, fits within the panel. The height of the person should be roughly 80-85% of the panel height as a guide. If the subject has wide arms or clothing, scale down the whole person uniformly. Do not slim the body or cut off edges to fit. Set placement guides at y=7.5% and y=92.5% within the panel coordinate system. These are invisible guides. Place the whole person within these guides. Center the silhouette at y=50% while maintaining aspect ratio. Ensure visible clear space above the head and below the feet. Do not allow contact with the panel edges. Blend brightness and tone without changing silhouettes, and add subtle, natural contact shadows at the feet. Do not redraw features for 3D effect.

[Separation of Subject and Text]
The left ~35% of each panel is for typography, and the right ~65% is for the person. Do not draw a dividing line. Keep the person on the right and text/shapes on the left, ensuring no overlap with the body. Leave a clear gap. If fit is difficult, prioritize uniform scaling of the person. 

[Typography Common Design]
Use the same condensed sans-serif font family, combining ultra-bold solid characters with bold outline characters. Design with size and layering without distorting characters. Use the following words: top left BOLD, top right COOL, bottom left PURE, bottom right EDGE. Use one main heading per panel, ensuring all letters are readable. Add one repeating outline of the same word as a supplementary element. Do not add other words or fine text. Maintain a clear size difference (helper text ~1.3-1.5x larger, in pale slate gray). Text overlaps should only happen in the left text area. No extreme perspective distortion or 3D effects. No barcodes or logos.

[Background and Color Palette]
Use bright backgrounds for all panels. Top left: ivory; Top right: cool gray; Bottom left: pale blue-gray; Bottom right: warm gray. Keep brightness levels similar. Avoid dark backgrounds. Use solid colors behind the person. Adjust brightness/warmth slightly to separate the silhouette naturally from the background. Main headings are ink black with vermilion red accents. Outlines are pale slate gray. Red is the same across all panels. Costume colors follow references.

[Composition of 4-Panel Text and Graphics]
Limit shapes to red rectangles and thin black lines. Strictly follow area separation. Create different compositions and centers of gravity for each panel.

Top Left - BOLD: Large solid text with offset outline overlap. Heading is BO/LD in two lines. Large black ultra-bold text occupies the upper-to-middle text area. One outline of BOLD is behind it, shifted slightly to the top left. Parts of the outline can be off-panel to the left.
